title: Minimum Threshold for K Inversion Pairs

notes.title: Original PDF
notes.html:
The problem as given on DomJudge:

prob-BIT.pdf

statement_html:
You are given an integer array nums and an integer k.

An inversion pair with threshold x is a pair of indices (i, j) such that i < j, nums[i] > nums[j], and nums[i] - nums[j] <= x.

Return the minimum integer min_threshold such that there are at least k inversion pairs with that threshold. If no such integer exists, return -1.

Input: the first line has n and k; the second line has nums.

Output: the minimum threshold, or -1.

Example 1:

Input:
7 7
1 2 3 4 3 2 1
Output: 2
Explanation: With x = 2 the valid pairs are (3,4), (2,5), (3,5), (4,5), (1,6), (2,6), (4,6), (5,6): 8 >= 7.
With x = 1 there are fewer than 7.

Example 2:

Input:
5 4
10 9 9 9 1
Output: 8
Explanation: With x = 8 the valid pairs are (0,1), (0,2), (0,3), (1,4), (2,4), (3,4): 6 >= 4.

Example 3:

Input:
3 4
3 2 1
Output: -1
Explanation: There are only 3 inversion pairs in total.

Constraints:

  • 1 <= n <= 104

  • 1 <= nums[i] <= 109

  • 1 <= k <= 109

Hint: the count of valid pairs grows with x, so binary search on x; count pairs with 0 < nums[i] - nums[j] <= x using a Fenwick tree over compressed values.
